result.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
result.summary: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). Two popular paradigms for improving the stability of learned dynamics are to train on interpolated or noisy samples or to regularize the Jacobian of the learned representation. In this work, we demonstrate that these paradigms can be understood under a common lens and that they both correspond to an approximation of the gradients obtained in an unrolled learning strategy. Building on this understanding, we derive a principled and complete approach to regularize training and demonstrate its impact on the stability of learned dynamical systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出，插值或加噪训练与表征 Jacobian 正则化可统一理解为对展开轨迹梯度学习的近似，并据此推导出更完整的正则化训练方案，以缓解神经动力系统长期积分的稳定性与精度问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「展开梯度近似」视角可能为 LVR 中循环/多步 latent 状态更新与轨迹训练提供可核查的稳定性与监督线索，但该分析面向连续动力系统，能否迁移到视觉推理的离散 latent 更新尚待判断。
